lead: Tesla / TSLA - Musk is back in charge
smaller: GameStop / GME - the meme stock is back
Silver / SLV - the squeeze is on
D-Wave / QBTS - quantum is the next AI
why_lead: Tesla combines the two signals the lead needs on this date: the stock closed up 15.61 percent over five sessions to 273.13 (still 3.13 percent lower over 20), and the attention headlines are loud, from Stocktwits winning-streak coverage and a $2,600 target from Cathie Wood to a top investor calling it a meme stock. The Musk-back-in-charge story is the simple narrative the crowd repeats, and the same feed carries the bear counter-narrative (owner offloading, protests, brand damage), which gives the When the Narrative Breaks section a real, dated tension.
why_smaller: GameStop is the second-strongest attention story with a violent price action: the shares fell 22.11 percent in the prior session on the bitcoin-pivot questions, after the 12 percent and 15 percent pops of the previous two sessions, and it gives a distinct crypto-treasury narrative.

Silver is the non-equity smaller trade, carried by a squeeze headline, a record gold print and a physical trust NAV headline, with SLV up 10.28 percent over 20 sessions and a clear 31.80 card reference to break.

D-Wave is the non-AI-infrastructure smaller trade: QBTS is up 44.96 percent over 20 sessions while down 7.25 percent over five, with several retail-attention pieces on quantum as the next AI, and its 5.56 reference gives a crisp break level.
considered_not_chosen: Nvidia: a -7.26 percent 20-session move and heavy AI attention, but its coverage is about the sector and May 15 rather than a single retail crowd trade, so it sits in the sector and catalyst sections instead.
Rivian: a 19.67 percent five-session surge with spin-off excitement, used only as a peer data point inside the Tesla lead because the attention is thinner than Tesla's.
Robinhood: heavy platform and product coverage, but a -9.82 percent 20-session move is not the surge or sharp drawdown the crowd is buying, so it fails the price-plus-attention test.
Oklo: a 26.46 percent 20-session drawdown with regulator news, used in catalysts as a bearish name rather than as a retail buy-the-dip trade.
Nebius: 20.72 percent lower over 20 sessions with a Reddit-ranked AI-pick headline, but the same AI-infrastructure theme as the sector section, so it was not given a separate slot.

Dogecoin and Shiba Inu: a Stocktwits retail-bullish headline and a double-digit five-session DOGE move, but the crypto retail attention is meme-coin noise rather than a single repeatable story with a card-level break point.
AppLovin: a 20.12 percent one-session fall with no explanatory headline in the window, so the narrative the crowd repeats could not be evidenced and it was dropped.
CoreWeave: pricing headlines dated March 27 and heavy pre-IPO retail interest, but the debut falls after the cutoff and the ticker is not in the card, so it was excluded.
Lululemon: results released after the US close on March 27 with the reaction on March 28, so the outcome is excluded as after the cutoff.
McCormick: a Reuters miss and a food-business outlook headline conflict on the same results, so no direction is given.
Shell and Nvidia earnings items: the feed dates them weeks after the events they describe, so they are treated as stale and not used as fresh results.
